d: Grenade. - Royal apartments in the Alhambra - in the middle of arches, where you can see the court of the Lions - the glow of burning flames in alabaster lamps mysteriously contrasts with the languorous light within that place suffused by the twilight of the Vespertine. On the one hand, under a rich pavilion, lies majesticly the Moor Boabdil king of Grenade; a man of strange appearance enveloped in black tunic appears in the bottom - is Issàchar, - guata around meditabundo, indi tra se:

While the King cries out of anguish and fury, at a nod of Issàchar, almost by enchantment, they appear from the middle arches of graceful Franciulle and Schiavi bringing guzles and other instruments; some dance, others playing accompanied by the following:

Garden surrounded by ruined walls in the most remote corner of Granata - Night - On one side, flanked by pomegranates and sycamores, stands an old house of bizarre architecture of epoch much before the Moorish domination, but on the style of this one, then rebuilt in part where it had collapsed - in the background, in waterproofing, pinacles and mosques with moonlight. Adèl-Muza enters guardingo in the garden, and turning to a veron of the house fieryly illuminated, sings:
Leila trepidating from the house, is said.
Leila fainted, then Issàchar from the hideout.

The inner place of the royal pavilion in the Spanish field awaited under Grenade - Everything lies in the utmost silence and darkness. Wrapped in brown hoods are the Judges of the Supreme Court, speaking in a quiet voice with mystery.
Ferdinand of Aragon, the Grand Judge, a Shielder.
Issàchar and Leila veiled are introduced.
The Judges and the Archers of the Supreme Court are coming out, who are about to bind Issachar; he is furious, imperishable, Leila is mute for fear.
Leila and Ferdinando.
Suddenly the Grand Judge, the Judges, the Archers come out of their courthouse in the utmost consternation, and said.

The trumpets are ringing, the field of every one where he wakes up; the tent is filled with Warriors, who run frightened, then Isabella of Castile, Dame Spagnole, Handmaids, Valletti, etc., etc., great is the turmoil, the terror.
They see the spaghetti curtains, full of fire, in the midst of which Issachar is seen from afar, wielding a burning torch in terrible action, crying out:

Underground in the home of Issàchar - the vast vaults crudely carved in the rock surmount informative and gigantic pillars, to which as trophies hang rusty weapons of a very remote epoch - here and there are in bulk instruments of alchemy of various and bizarre forms - a huge metal lamp rusted hangs from above, blazing the place of magical and wild appearance. Issàchar and various his Family are intent on sharpening and supplying weapons; from there a few moments a romantic outside is heard. Issàchar goes to the bottom, and spy for a foram.
Issàchar presses a stone, which, turning slightly over a spring, opens the entrance to Men of various countries gathered there with torches underground.

Pavilion in a forest near the Spanish camp; the bottom is open, and between the thick of the bush you can see from a distance the golden cocuzzoli of Granata. Strepito, warlike sounds, and festive voices in the distance.

At the sound of a joyful music, the Spanish army proceeds, at the head of which the Gonfalonieri, with the insignia of Aragon, Castile, Calatrava, Ferdinando, Isabella, the Grand Judge and the royal court, are first difficult.
A call announces the Moorish embassy, Adèl-Muza is at the head of it; he is dignified, haughty; all open to him with regard to the way.

A romantic wooded valley in the Andalusian mountains - it is at the end of the night - of a façade, shaded by old oaks, stands an old abbey, on whose black walls the moon still spreads a fievol light; it reigns deep calm; that holy asylum seems uninhabited. After several singings of sacred ringing light gradually inside the temple, and come out in a long processional stuo from adjacent cloister Hermits and Matrons.
Ferdinand of Aragon, Leila, Isabella of Castile, and Followed by the cloister.
On the vestibule of the abbey are the Hermits, the Grand Judge and the veiled Matrons.
The place remains deserted a few moments, then Adèl-Muza, disguised in brown armor shaped like Spanish.
And a man in a torn robe, which was pierced for a long way, shall come forth as a beast of the plants, and he is Issachar.

Smurfing with brutal joy Issàchar leaves the temple, passing the pale daughter, and on the steps of the threshold he pierces her; then Ferdinand of Aragon, Isabella of Castile, the Great Judge and the religious mat, rush into pale confusion of terror, and consternation.
